LESSON: KITCHEN AND BACKYARD GARDENING (SOWING TRANSPLANTING, WATERING REAPING, PLUCKING, WHEELBARROW AND TROWELS.)

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: FOOD PRODUCTION PROCESSES Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested
Topic 2.1: Kitchen and backyard gardening (Sowing transplanting, watering reaping, plucking, wheelbarrow and trowels.)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 9

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Kitchen and backyard gardening (Sowing transplanting, watering reaping, plucking, wheelbarrow and trowels.), part of FOOD PRODUCTION PROCESSES Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8 AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How does a kitchen garden contribute to food production?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Kitchen and backyard gardening (Sowing transplanting, watering reaping, plucking, wheelbarrow and trowels.) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Responsibility: The learner recognizes their role in providing food security through developing kitchen/backyard gardens to enhance

food production.

● Unity: The learner collaborates with peers to establish and manage a kitchen or backyard garden within the school environment.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Health promotion: The learner understands the need for fresh food produced in a clean environment for healthy functioning of the body.

● Disaster and risk reduction: The learner understands the need for kitchen gardening to reduce food insecurity that leads to hunger and

starvation.

12

Link to other subjects:

● Learners relate growing of own food in kitchen or backyard garden to financial literacy skills learnt in Pre-technical studies.

● Gardening tools and equipment - Watering cans, Jembe

• Learning to learn: The learner enhances investigation skills as they take an expedition in the school community to observe the kitchen

garden.

• Critical thinking and problem-solving skills: The learner enhances open mindedness and creativity as they take into account other

possibilities and points of view as they carry out an activity to establish a kitchen or backyard garden

• Digital literacy: The learner practises digital citizenship as they observe safety precautions when using digital media to search for words

related to kitchen and backyard gardening in food production.
